name: catalog-vault-first-fetch
comment: Data-vault adoption Slice 4 (2026-08-22), Session 2. Proves the runtime-validation claim this slice exists for: a machine with an empty tagged AppData root AND no reachable local data/*.db (both dev-relative-path rungs of resolveCatalogPath's ladder defeated by running a scratch copy of the runtime tree two directory levels deep from any data/ sibling) fetches the four catalogue dbs from the real public GitHub release (kingoftheseas56/Colosseum-Data) and wakes the Tankoban surfaces once they land. Live network, not a deterministic gate -- run with a long ui-wait-for budget. The onboarding step order is copied from the Slice 3 ledger entry; the downloading-line/masthead assertions are new to this slice.

steps.label: the session answers, drive gated on
one visible window, isolated data root
the boot splash has left the screen
a fresh tag gates world content behind account onboarding
first-launch fetch: the vault client starts pulling the real release (no data/ sibling reachable from this scratch runtime tree)
enter Tankoban while the fetch is still in flight
Hemanth's ratification exhibit: the empty Tankoban wall shows the honest downloading line
all four catalogue dbs have landed (long budget: ~150MB over real network, measured ~700KB/s on this machine)
fetching has settled false now that every catalog is ready
the same surface, now populated (wake-on-ready proof)
a real MAL-backed discover card exists post-fetch (One Piece, malId 13)
open One Piece via the top-manga rail
masthead identity confirms the fetched db is genuine (One Piece, malId 13)
